correctness.rationale: The full pinned facet enumeration agrees with Ahmad–Fourier–Joswig Lemma 3.2 for maximal ranked posets. Dirichlet integration over per-rank coordinate maxima gives common volume ∏m_i!/n! including singleton and endpoint cases. Each chain zero-facet rank sums to nV, the top x=1 rank to nV, each order cover interface to nV√2 by identifying two coordinates, and the unique mixed chain-to-order facet family to nV√(k+1) by graph-coordinate Gram determinant and beta integrals. Summing yields S_k/V=n[k+1+√(k+1)+(r−k−1)√2] and pure chain endpoint n(r+√r). Differences for k≤r−2 are 1−√2+√(k+2)−√(k+1), zero at k=0, negative at k≥1; final difference is zero. r=1,2 also checked separately, including singleton ranks. Independent direct evaluation for r=1..8 confirmed equality and monotone order; this finite check is not the all-r proof.

Published metric results for pure order and pure chain endpoints establish S_0 and S_r under narrower nonsingleton assumptions; neither determines intermediate k nor covers the full singleton-inclusive rank interpolation. value.rationale: Boundary measure is a natural first Euclidean Steiner invariant of volume-equivalent poset polytopes. The complete intermediate profile and its strict reversal relative to face-count monotonicity answer a structural metric question for all rank populations, not a mere endpoint substitution or routine f-vector calculation.

final_claim: For every ordinal sum of r positive antichains of total size n>=2, the canonical Euclidean chain–order interpolating K_k have common volume ∏m_i!/n! and exact normalized surface areas n(k+1+sqrt(k+1)+(r-k-1)sqrt2) for k<r and n(r+sqrt r) at k=r, independent of individual rank populations, with S_0=S_1>S_2>...>S_{r-1}=S_r for r>=3.
limitations: Does not determine higher Steiner coefficients or arbitrary ranked-poset families.
R=1,2 equalities and singleton boundary cases incorporated; no claim of historical-priority certainty.
